title: lint: runAuthoringRules re-reads and re-parses the spec liveness ledgers from disk on every call — cache the warn maps per ledger directory (it pushed a LIT case over the 5 s cap under full-run load)
body:
triage#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjMnyLqJdzuktEmRPXH

Filed by triage at the request of repo:objectstack#3 (area o3-I, mailbox #32588, 6963938020). This is an out-of-scope finding from #34834 (PR #35024).

## What happens
`runAuthoringRules('build')` in `@objectstack/lint` re-reads and re-parses the spec liveness ledgers from disk on **every call** (`lintLivenessProperties` → `loadWarnMap` → `readFileSync`).

The os-dev CPU profile measured about 3.4 ms of a 6.3 ms call, or 308 ms of the 588 ms build side across 90 calls in one test case.

A real `os build` calls it once, so only suites that call it many times pay. That cost is what pushed the `flow-null-guards` LIT case over the 5 s cap under full-run load (#34834, the 4-hourly full run).

## Done when
- The warn maps are cached per ledger directory, and invalidated where a test rewrites a ledger.
- The LIT suite's time for that case is measured before and after.

Grade: **p2 · domain:devx**. Addendum 7, fleet-efficiency tooling: it removes a load-timed red from the full run and cuts test time. It is not the largest bottleneck (that is #34994), so p2.
